instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/tests/pages.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. blocker (line 118): Typecheck regression (baseline was exit 0). addElementsFromPasteOrLibrary takes one opts object { elements, files, position: {clientX, clientY} | 'cursor' | 'center' }, not (elements, { position }). In the same test, `new Pointer('mouse').click(10, 10)` with the rectangle tool makes a zero-size rectangle, and App removes it as invisibly small, so `drawn.length` is 0. — fix: Call `act(() => h.app.addElementsFromPasteOrLibrary({ elements: [pasteRect], files: null, position: 'center' }))`. Draw with down(10,10) then up(40,40), or use UI.createElement, instead of click().
2. blocker (line 334): Typecheck regression: exportScene's data.appState is ReturnType<typeof cleanAppStateForExport>, and spreading the full h.state does not type-check. The test also fails at runtime. rect2 is added through API.setElements (h.elements setter -> replaceAllElements, no stamping), so it has no pageId and lands on the home page, not page 2. The SVG assertion (a string match on attribute order) is also too weak to prove only one rectangle was exported. — fix: Pass `appState: { ...cleanAppStateForExport(h.state), exportBackground: true, viewBackgroundColor: '#ffffff' }`. Create rect2 with `pageId: h.state.activePageId`, or add it via API.updateScene with captureUpdate IMMEDIATELY so it is stamped. Assert that the exported element count / element ids equal [rect2.id].
3. blocker (line 89): Several tests call h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionSwitchPage, ...) outside act() (lines 89, 204, 231, 258, 502). With the concurrent root used by test-utils, setState is not flushed before the following assertions run. Existing suites (e.g. stickyNotes.test.tsx:288) wrap these calls in act(). This is the probable cause of the 'viewport per page', 'undo stays on its page' and 'whole-scene updateScene keeps pageId' failures (medium confidence). 'only the active page is rendered and selectable' (line 73) also adds rect2 via API.setElements with no pageId, so rect2 lands on the home page. — fix: Wrap every direct executeAction call in act() (or add an API.executeAction(action, value) helper that does). In the selection test, give rect2 `pageId: page2Id` (or add it through API.updateScene with IMMEDIATELY).
4. blocker (line 455): 'search switches to the page of a result' queries data-testid 'search-menu-input', which does not exist anywhere in SearchMenu.tsx, so waitFor times out. Even with the input found, focusIndex starts null after a search, so the page-switch effect never runs until a match is focused. — fix: Find the input by its existing selector (e.g. the TextField placeholder/role, or add a data-testid to the SearchMenu TextField). After typing, focus the first match by pressing Enter (goToNextItem) or clicking the result, then wait for activePageId === page1Id.
5. minor: Coverage gaps against U22: drag-and-drop reorder, Escape cancelling a rename, and view mode (only switching offered; no create, delete or rename) have no tests. — fix: Add jsdom cases: fireEvent.dragStart/drop between tabs, Escape on page-rename-input, and viewModeEnabled hiding page-create/page-delete while tab clicks still switch.

Fix `packages/element/src/pages.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. minor (line 356): restorePages accepts any non-empty string as index. generateKeyBetween throws on keys that are not valid fractional indices, so a malformed file or remote payload (e.g. index '0' or 'zz') makes createPage/reorderPage throw later, even though restore is meant to never throw. — fix: Validate each index (try generateKeyBetween(index, null) in a try/catch, or reuse the element package's fractional-index validation) and generate a fresh key after the previous kept page when it is invalid.
2. minor (line 104): getScenePageOptions keeps a single-entry memo at module level. With two <Excalidraw> instances mounted on one page, every render alternates the cached arguments and returns a new object. Scene.setActivePage then recomputes the page caches and regenerates sceneNonce on every render (defeats NFR-2 and invalidates renderer caches). — fix: Key the memo per pages array (WeakMap<pages, {activePageId, options}>) or hold the last options on the Scene/App instance instead of module scope.
